scenes.title: Charging a Capacitor
scenes.topic: RC circuits — charging curve, time constant τ = RC

scenes.title: Moment of Inertia
scenes.topic: Moment of inertia — I = mr², quadratic radius scaling, disk integral I = ½MR²

scenes.title: Hoop vs Disk: Why a Disk Wins
scenes.topic: Rolling without slipping — energy conservation gives v = √(2gh / (1 + I/MR²)); disk beats hoop because less inertia goes into rotation

scenes.title: Hooke's Law: Why a Spring Bobs
scenes.topic: Simple harmonic motion of a spring — Hooke's law F = -kx leads to ω₀ = √(k/m) and period T = 2π√(m/k)

scenes.title: The Simple Pendulum: Why Mass Doesn't Matter
scenes.topic: Simple pendulum — for small swings, T = 2π√(L/g); the period depends on length and gravity, not mass

scenes.title: RLC and Pendulum: Same Math, Different Physics
scenes.topic: RLC ↔ pendulum analogy — both obey the same second-order linear ODE, with q↔x, I↔v, L↔m, 1/C↔k, R↔b

scenes.title: Centripetal Acceleration: Steering, Not Speeding
scenes.topic: Centripetal acceleration — uniform circular motion gives a = v²/r = rω², always pointing toward the centre

scenes.title: Steiner's Theorem: The Cost of an Off-Centre Axis
scenes.topic: Parallel-axis (Steiner's) theorem — I = I_cm + Md², the moment of inertia about any axis equals the inertia about a parallel axis through the centre of mass plus M times the squared offset

scenes.title: Damped Oscillation: Why Real Springs Stop
scenes.topic: Damped harmonic oscillator — adding velocity-proportional drag turns Hooke's law into m·ẍ + b·ẋ + k·x = 0; underdamped solution x(t) = A·e^(-γt)·sin(ωt+φ); regimes: underdamped, critically damped, overdamped

scenes.title: Torque: Why Leverage Beats Force
scenes.topic: Torque (Dreiemoment) — τ = rF sin θ; only the perpendicular component of a force creates rotation, peaking at θ = 90° and vanishing when force is parallel to the lever arm

scenes.title: Coulomb's Law: The Inverse-Square Tug
scenes.topic: Coulomb's law — F = k·q₁q₂/r²; force scales with the product of charges and the inverse square of distance; like repels, opposite attracts

scenes.title: Virtualizing the CPU: One Processor, Many Programs
scenes.topic: CPU virtualization — the OS gives each process the illusion of its own CPU by time-slicing one physical processor and performing context switches

scenes.title: fork(): One Process Becomes Two
scenes.topic: fork() duplicates the calling process — both parent and child return from the same call with different return values, and run concurrently from there

scenes.title: User Mode and Kernel Mode: The Trap Door
scenes.topic: User mode vs kernel mode — programs run directly on the CPU in user mode; a trap instruction is the only legal way to reach the kernel for privileged work, and a return-from-trap brings the CPU back

scenes.title: Round-Robin Scheduling: Fairness by the Slice
scenes.topic: Round-robin scheduling — give every ready job one fixed-length time slice in turn; short jobs respond fast, long jobs make steady progress

scenes.title: Address Translation: How a Page Table Finds the Bytes
scenes.topic: Paging address translation — a virtual address splits into VPN + offset; the VPN indexes a per-process page table to a physical frame number; the frame number plus the offset is the physical address

scenes.title: Race Condition: When Two Threads Share a Counter
scenes.topic: Race condition — two threads incrementing a shared counter can interleave their load-add-store steps so an increment is silently lost; fixing it needs a critical section

scenes.title: Test-and-Set: Building a Lock with One Atomic Instruction
scenes.topic: Test-and-set lock — a single atomic hardware instruction reads a flag's old value and writes one in the same step; threads that read zero own the lock, threads that read one spin until it is released

scenes.title: Address Space: Where Your Program Lives in Memory
scenes.topic: Address space layout — every process sees a virtual memory region with code at the bottom, static data above it, the heap growing up via malloc, and the stack growing down on each function call

scenes.title: The Inode: A File's Map to Its Blocks
scenes.topic: Inodes — every file has a fixed-size record holding its metadata and a list of pointers to the disk blocks that contain its bytes; direct pointers handle small files in one hop, indirect pointers fan out to reach large files via a tree of block pointers

scenes.title: Shortest Job First: Why Order Changes Wait Time
scenes.topic: Shortest Job First scheduling — three jobs arrive together; running them in arrival order versus shortest-first changes the average turnaround time even though the total work is identical

scenes.title: Producer–Consumer: When a Thread Needs to Wait
scenes.topic: Producer–consumer with condition variables — a bounded buffer fills and drains; a producer that finds the buffer full waits on a condition; a consumer that finds it empty waits on the other; signal wakes one waiter

scenes.title: TLB Hits and Misses: The Cost of a Page Table Lookup
scenes.topic: Translation Lookaside Buffer — a tiny on-chip cache of recent virtual-to-physical translations; a hit returns the frame number in a single cycle, a miss walks the page table and then fills the cache, dramatically slower

scenes.title: Semaphores: A Counter Threads Wait On
scenes.topic: Semaphores — a single integer plus a queue: P() decrements and blocks if the value would go negative, V() increments and wakes a waiter; a semaphore with initial value 1 acts as a lock

scenes.title: Process States: Running, Ready, Blocked
scenes.topic: Process states — a process is always in one of three states: RUNNING on the CPU, READY waiting for the CPU, or BLOCKED waiting on an I/O completion; the scheduler and I/O events drive every transition

scenes.title: Polling vs Interrupts: How the CPU Talks to a Slow Disk
scenes.topic: Polling vs interrupts — polling spins the CPU on a device status register until the device is ready; an interrupt lets the CPU run other work and be woken when the device is done. For a slow device the difference is most of the CPU's time.
